# Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka (Kd 3)
**ID:** Kd 3
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka* is the third chapter of the Khandhaka section of the Vinaya Piṭaka, situated in the *Mahāvagga* between the *Uposathakkhandhaka* and the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* [Frauwallner 1956; Norman 1983]. The text prohibits Buddhist monastics from traveling during the three months of the rainy season, instituting the compulsory observance of the rains retreat (*vassa*) in an appropriate residence [SuttaCentral]. The traditional justification for restricting travel during the rains—avoiding injury to small creatures and sprouting plant life—is an ancient Vinaya rationale shared with parallel traditions [Bechert 1992]. Commentarial analysis in the *Samantapāsādikā* observes that within this chapter, the only category of ecclesiastical offence laid down for breaches of its regulations is that of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) [Horner 1966].
Curated parallels to the *Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka* survive in other early Vinaya lineages under the title *Varṣāvastu*, extant in Sanskrit (Mūlasarvāstivāda), Tibetan, and several Chinese translations of the Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka recensions [SuttaCentral; Frauwallner 1956; Bechert 1992]. In automated analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shows heavy internal phrase reuse with neighbouring Khandhaka sections—particularly the *Uposathakkhandhaka* (Kd 2) and *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4)—as well as later Vinaya manuals such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations have been produced by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner 1966; SuttaCentral].
